prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1289; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the photographs submitted by the other driver. Both the witnesses and the other driver describe the collision the same way, and the damage on the claimant's vehicle lines up with the reported impact point.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time and reported neck and back strain. The described injury is consistent with a lateral impact of this kind.

Entry 4: Obtained the claimant's medical records. Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits tapering as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records.

Entry 5: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account matched the account given at first notice and in earlier conversations with the claimant.

Entry 6: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage period, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 7: Reviewed the repair estimate against the photographs and the reported point of impact. The line items align with the damage pattern, and no unrelated components have been added.

Entry 8: File is progressing normally. Liability appears clear based on the police report, witness statements and the other driver's account, and the bodily injury component is being evaluated against the completed treatment records.
